commitResults.messageTitle: Find students by part of their name with n/
commitResults.messageBody:
find matches only whole words in a student's name, so a tutor who
remembers only part of a name, such as "avi" for David, gets no
results. This is the case UC4 covers: finding a student quickly while
a guardian is on the phone.

Change find to take a single n/ value and match it anywhere in the
name, ignoring case. The value is matched as one piece of text, so
"loe tan" finds Chloe Tan but "tan loe" does not. Runs of spaces in
the value are squeezed to one.

Reject a blank value, because every name contains the empty string
and the search would match every student. Reject a repeated n/ and
any text before it, so a mistyped command shows an error instead of
silently searching for something else.

Lowercase with Locale.ROOT, so the result does not depend on the
computer's language setting. In a Turkish locale, "IDA" lowercases
to "ıda", and find would miss a student named Ida.

The name predicate keeps its list of keywords, although the parser
now always passes one. Changing its constructor would touch test
files that open PRs are also editing, so that cleanup is left for
after they merge.

commitResults.messageTitle: Developer Guide: Add filter implementation section
commitResults.messageBody:
Explain how filter parses its prefixes, builds one predicate per
filter, and combines them with AND, and why fields match partially
or exactly.

Filter students by school and combine filters

filter now accepts more than one prefix and shows only students who
match every filter given:

* sch/SCHOOL matches any part of the school, ignoring case and
  extra spaces. n/NAME works as before.
* Each filter is its own predicate. StudentMatchesAllPredicate
  combines them with AND, so lvl/, sub/, p/, gn/ and gp/ can be
  added the same way.
* FilterCommandParser takes several prefixes. It needs at least one
  filter, rejects repeated prefixes and text before the first one,
  and gives a specific message for each blank value.
* t/ and nid/ are rejected with a message that filter cannot search
  notes, instead of being read as part of another value.
* New StringUtil#containsIgnoreCaseAndSpaces for partial matching.
* The User Guide filter section is now a table of filters with an
  error table.

Moving forward, will add findnote functionality into filter as well.

Tutors plan lessons one level at a time. filter now takes lvl/LEVEL,
checked with the same rules as add, so lvl/s3 works and lvl/S6 gives
the level constraint message. Level combines with the other filters.

commitResults.messageTitle: Read everything after note/ as note text in filter

addnote does, so any note text can be searched. Filters after note/
are now read as part of the note text.
